snippet.textDisplay:
Speaking of a narcissistic sibling being the distorter of history….. my little sister is six years younger than me, her being 63 and me being 70 now. Up to this day, she still distorts her childchildhood stories to make herself sound like a victim her older sister never wanted around. She says, “Yeah….I remember when mom would make you take care of me and you would always RUN FROM ME with your other friends.” Fact is I was 9 years old and when we would decide to go to the swing set or something and RUN to it she would always cry like a brat because she couldn’t run as fast. She says, “Remember when you chopped all my hair off because you were jealous of my long hair?” The fact was I was 16 at this point and I cut everybody’s hair at school when the short style of one side longer than the other side was popular. I even cut the football team’s hair. She wanted her hair like everybody else’s and so I cut it for her (with mom’s permission mind you). To her disappointment she was shocked to the core having her hair gone and blamed me for it…. and to this day, my mother says she never gave me permission. Yet if there is something, my mother doesn’t want to be responsible for she always reminds us that she’s 90 and her memory is gone. They BOTH make it IMPOSSIBLE to love them. I was always skinnier and more confident. I was a cheerleader and had boyfriends. She was heavy, an introvert with glasses and always envied me. I have just always wanted to have a sister relationship with her, but the truth is, as Dr Ramani says, if she wasn’t my sister I would never choose to like her as my friend. My narcissistic mother always, and to this day makes it my responsibility to make her feel better about herself. I always have to be the one to call her and drive across the country to visit her and to play down any successes in my life when I’m in a family setting so as to not upset her. I have, by the way called BS on all of this…. At least in my own mind, heart and behavior. I have gone all but no contact because my mother is after all 90 at this point.
To this day, her being the golden child, has managed to gaslight my mother (a narcissist herself, who should be quite aware of the manipulation) into leaving her entire estate (which is in the millions) to her, leaving the other four children completely out. It has been heartbreaking. This is a narcissistic family that I could write a book on but I will leave it with this…. Dr. Ramani is right….. all the way right!
